column4: All finite abelian groups and all n-vertex trees require a complete obstruction classification. Source Theorem 1 classifies sufficiently large bounded-degree trees only; its core absorption theorem does not remove bounded degree or small n. Enumerating a few trees cannot close either gap.

A construction gives density 5/9 but the universal asymptotic upper bound for every tetrahedron-free 3-graph is missing. Source explicitly distinguishes tight-cycle results from this tetrahedron. Finite forbidden-subgraph checks or a lower-bound construction do not prove the matching upper bound.

The target ranges over all n,m. Source Theorem 2 already supplies asymptotically correct estimates in the exponential m regime and Theorem 3 addresses a bipartite regime. A new estimate without a specified improvement would merely restate source progress; exact optima require controlling every set family.

All n,r maximum cardinalities require matching constructions and upper bounds. Source records an exponential-rate logarithmic gap between cover-free upper and lower bounds; its tight sampling-probability lemma does not close the extremal-code gap. Small disjunct matrices are instances only.

Generic linear versus formal generic projections must agree for arbitrary dimensionality type. Source settles types 1 and 2 and explains why transversality alone fails; type at least 3 needs control of iterated discriminants, not another low-type example.

The record asks all normal rank-one del Pezzo surfaces and all singularity types. The report's Theorem 1 already lists cardinalities for the log-canonical classification it discusses, including positive-dimensional moduli. Resolve the missing singularity hypotheses and audit cited tables before claiming a new uniqueness result; a single surface is insufficient.

Source Corollary 1 already produces complements for finite left braces and normal complements when the ideal is two-sided. Need a genuinely additional class with a conjugation-invariant complement; abelian groups and circle groups are source-internal public cases. Checking finite brace multiplication does not certify all integral units.

Need classify all objects, endomorphisms and associative/coassociative splitting data in both completions. Definition 1 requires a separable nonunital algebra-coalgebra structure. The stated equivalence between completions is not an explicit classification; finding one idempotent is not full scope.

Need a discrete base representation with a defined wrinkle-free invariant preserved by dynamics for complex wrinkle fields. Source reports aliasing and suggests spline/subdivision alternatives without an invariant or theorem. Filtering a mesh in an example would be a numerical implementation, not the requested general guarantee.

Least f(d,s,t) requires both universal partitions and matching point configurations for all parameters. Source defines s-convex as union of s convex sets and already discusses a solution to the existence generalization. Ordinary Radon handles s=t=1 only; it does not supply optimality or polynomial dependence in arbitrary s,t.

Literal r=1 includes complete graphs, because linearity of 2-uniform graphs does not imply triangle-freeness. Source moves from uncrowded hypergraphs to the claimed linear bound and invokes Shearer for graphs. Clique sanity check exposes a missing-scope issue, not discovery credit. For intended higher-uniform or uncrowded targets the source identifies the random-independent-set shadow expectation as an obstacle; do not silently repair hypotheses.

Diameter multiplicity is already at most n. Need a second distinct distance of multiplicity at most n for every nonconvex n-point set, n>4. Source reports the convex-position case solved; a regular polygon or sampled point set only reconfirms instances and cannot control arbitrary incidence patterns.

The largest m depends on vocabulary size, embedding dimension, and strict ranking conventions omitted in the record. Source gives random-matrix bounds and sign-rank bounds for trained matrices. Shattering every m-subset by logits is a uniform separability problem; one top-m set or a full-rank unrestricted matrix bypasses the intended bottleneck and earns no credit.

TP(X) is an exponent supremum with a single C uniform over x,y and finite F, not a ratio for one tour. Source gives d/(2d-1) for Euclidean median examples and 1 for hyperbolic graphs; a product of branching trees needs matching growth exponents and degree/product conventions. A tree factor or small grid does not determine the product invariant.

Need a constant-relative-gap local-Hamiltonian QMA-hardness reduction under quantum polynomial-time reductions. Source Conjecture 1.3 distinguishes inverse-polynomial absolute gap from linear-in-terms gap. A classical PCP or one Hamiltonian energy calculation cannot amplify a general noncommuting quantum instance with bounded locality.

Exact nonuniform worst-case NP not in P/poly to distributional AvgP implication needs reductions controlling every relevant efficiently samplable distribution and algorithm convention. The record cites Bogdanov-Trevisan but its primary body was not obtained; assumptions such as iO cannot be substituted. No verified reduction or bounded decisive test is available.

Need deterministic O(log n) workspace for every bounded-error polynomial-time logspace computation. Source weighted pseudorandom generators are not automatically ordinary generators or an exact-space derandomization. Must account for seed enumeration, signed weights and numerical evaluation space; finite branching-program agreement cannot prove the universal simulation.

Exact 4/3 gap needs all symmetric metrics and matching extremal families. The cited source concerns 1,2-TSP, a restricted metric class; primary theorem and general-case successor audit are missing. A finite LP instance certifies only a lower bound, not the universal rounding inequality.

All bounded C*-algebra representations need one bounded invertible conjugator yielding a star representation. A matrix-algebra argument does not cover arbitrary Hilbert-space dimension or arbitrary C*-algebras; a uniform completely-boundedness bridge would be needed. Thesis primary passage and successor audit are missing.

Every finite-VC class requires an O(d) realizable compression scheme with bounded side information. Source explicitly gives existing exponential-in-VC bounds and conditional reductions from binary compression, not the conjectured linear compressor. A scheme for a special class or a reduction assuming the target is no resolution.

All nonamenable Cayley graphs require a strict nonuniqueness interval, not just selected generating sets or tree examples. Need compare percolation thresholds and quantify over groups and generators. Primary survey passage and closest general successor were not obtained; status text in the corpus is not proof.

Need volume injective on both hyperbolic and spherical Dehn kernels. Source Conjecture 1.3 separates this from the Euclidean theorem and countability/image results. Computing Dehn invariants of finitely many polyhedra cannot rule out a global kernel element of zero volume.

Order of limits fixes r before n tends to infinity and then sends r to infinity. Need a lower bound diverging uniformly over all covering linear codes in each fixed-radius asymptotic. Perfect radius-one Hamming codes or finite covering-code enumerations do not control this iterated limit.

For every field and dimension, every invertible I+H with quadratic homogeneous H must admit elementary/affine factorization. Source Conjecture 4.2 follows low-dimensional finite-field computations; invertibility cannot be inferred from homogeneity alone despite record wording. Enumerating finite-field maps or bounded factor lengths cannot establish tameness in arbitrary dimension and characteristic.

Target includes an infinite practical-number assertion and subpolynomial factorial divisor-sum length. Source already records Vose's square-root upper bound. Need a uniform sparse distinct-divisor representation for every residue below n!, not small factorial decompositions; quantifiers in epsilon and n must be retained.

Three scopes: O(sqrt N), exact maximization by 24n+1 for every N>6, and uniqueness up to the stated equivalence at pentagonal endpoints. Sieve counts in one progression cannot bound unbounded q,a; small searches cannot prove any universal form. Wikipedia record alone leaves primary conventions and successor results unresolved.

Need a disjoint subfamily retaining at least a quarter of union area for arbitrary sizes plus a sharp family approaching the quarter bound. Greedy packing estimates with dilated squares lose constants, and equal-square tests miss mixed scales. Primary passage and sharp-constant successor audit absent; no bound claimed.

Equality of optimal triangular-container side lengths for every triangular n requires a lower bound for all packings of n-1 disks. Deleting a disk only gives one inequality; lattice configurations do not prove optimality. Primary source and successors missing, so finite coordinate packings are not an investable full-scope certificate.

Determine radii and optimal centers for every n, equivalently the full step function N(epsilon). A covering configuration gives only an upper bound; a matching continuous global lower bound is needed for each n. Exact small-n disks would be instances, and primary geometric conventions were not audited.

Every integer dimension needs sharp upper and lower spherical-code bounds. An explicit configuration proves only a lower bound; one-dimensional or known exceptional-dimension solutions leave arbitrary d untouched. Primary survey and closest dimension-independent successors missing; do not infer novelty from the index.

Every k needs a realizable straight-line arrangement and a matching upper bound on maximum disjoint triangles. The record counts arbitrary nonoverlapping triangular regions, so face-count bounds require a reduction before reuse. Primary definition and successor audit missing; a small arrangement supplies only an instance.

For each d require all general-position 2d+1-point configurations projectively convexifiable plus a nonconvexifiable 2d+2-point witness. This needs a uniform oriented-matroid or hyperplane-separation argument in all dimensions. Checking one planar configuration does not cover universal d; primary target and public-status audit missing.

All n exact maxima and all equality configurations are both required. Pair counting only gives the displayed upper bound and cannot characterize real collinearity extremizers. Large-n cubic constructions or asymptotic theorems leave finite exceptions and classification; primary and successors missing, no partial credit.

For every closed forest including unbounded sets, a rectifiable escape path need not exist: F=R^2 contains every curve. This only exposes a domain/attainment issue, excluded from discovery credit. Even bounded convex forests require shape-dependent minimax length and attainment, not an arbitrary long segment. Primary source missing; no repaired target substituted.

Need exact maximum chromatic number of a union of two planar graphs, with matching universal coloring and lower-bound example. Product of two four-colorings yields a coarse bound only; checking cliques does not supply the optimum. The map equivalence and primary best bounds were not audited.

For every proper minor-closed family and every positive weighting need a distortion bound depending only on the family. Tree embeddings or metrics of one forbidden-minor graph do not control arbitrary n and aspect ratios. Need a uniform cut-metric decomposition; primary theorem and successors missing.

Need every connected finite graph with a finite planar local-bijection cover to embed in the projective plane. Constructing a two-ply cover of a projective graph proves the opposite direction only. All higher-ply covers require an obstruction reduction; primary and successor evidence missing.

Bundled target asks exact degree-diameter optimum for all d,k, asymptotic Moore saturation for each k, and the 57-regular 3250-vertex Moore graph. BFS gives only the Moore upper bound; a few near-Moore graphs resolve none of these full scopes. Primary passage and current status missing, so park without construction search.

Equilateral triangle gives sharp lower ratio 2/sqrt(3), but every finite planar terminal set needs the matching Steiner/MST inequality. Verifying one topology or one triangle cannot control all Steiner trees. Primary proof-history and validity audit missing; do not treat the corpus equality as a verified theorem.

All r-partite r-uniform hypergraphs require tau <= (r-1)nu. Source gives only historical context and intersecting cases; matching number one and small r do not imply arbitrary matching number. A general transversal extraction argument is missing and successor status remains HOLD.

The literal positive-density arithmetic-progression assertion is the named public Szemeredi theorem, not a discovery lead. Primary proof body was not fetched, so this is an unverified public-result lead for root rather than a certified source/proof audit. No attempt to repackage density increment or finite checks as new credit.

Every k exact divisor-error exponent requires cancellation in zeta(s)^k estimates, including k=2. Computing d_k up to a cutoff cannot bound error for all x or identify the infimum exponent. The displayed Perron formula also needs endpoint conventions; repairing it is no credit. Primary and successor audit missing.

Santos 1006.2814v3 explicitly gives a bounded 43-dimensional polytope with 86 facets and diameter at least 44, violating 86-43=43. The source states the complete counterexample scope; no construction replay or full dependency audit was performed. Reusing this published witness cannot be a new result.

Need convergence of both normalized diameter and typical distance to distinct positive constants for each m>=2 and -m<delta<0 in the exact PA model. Source gives growth-order bounds but no typical lower bound. A 2019 diameter paper surfaced as a successor lead, not an audited body; simulations cannot prove convergence or transfer among PA variants.

Csaba Conjecture 13 matches the corpus; Bottcher-Schacht-Taraz Theorem 1 (author PDF dated 2008-08-12) supplies the same parameter order and spanning embedding. Apply with actual chromatic number <=r, whose minimum-degree requirement is weaker. This is a public resolution; proof dependencies include regularity and blow-up machinery, not replayed here.

Existential fixed t with eventual all-interior log-concavity is stronger than a limiting distribution or unimodality. Source Conjecture 4.2 already contains the t=75 numerical suggestion and unusual n(n-2) index cutoff. Need uniform local coefficient estimates through bulk and boundary; finite polynomial checks cannot prove eventual quantifiers or minimality.

Every pair of bounded-doubling graph families needs expected O(log n) greedy routing under a random permutation, with fixed doubling constants. Source Conjecture 7.1 distinguishes half-greedy and ordinary greedy routing and identifies edge dependence. Connectivity or empirical short paths do not bound the adaptive route uniformly.

Source defines deficiency as inf(relators-generators), explicitly warning of the opposite convention; corpus defines max(generators-relators) but keeps the positive-divergence conclusion. This sign reversal is a transcription issue, not a discovery. Intended Conjecture 6.1 is linked to relation-gap obstacles and cannot be resolved by computing one RAAG presentation.

Need O(r) edges for every r with r-partite intersection and transversal number at least r-1; source already proves the linear lower bound and small-r constructions. Truncated projective planes are too dense and only certain orders. Need a uniform sparse family and a transversal lower certificate, not another fixed r example.

Need central-binomial many pairwise path-different permutations for every n; the source already gives the central-binomial upper bound. Collision means consecutive values at a common coordinate, not shared consecutive patterns. A clique search for one n does not give a uniform construction attaining the bound; closest successor status remains unaudited.
